exceptions.title: Missing source evidence
exceptions.symptom: A required record is missing or cannot be located.
exceptions.example: The invoice is available, but the applicable authorization record is not.
exceptions.action: Identify the missing record, assign an owner and confirm it through an approved source before deciding whether the claim needs correction.
exceptions.evidence: Record type, source owner and the applicable requirement.
exceptions.avoid: Missing evidence is a question to investigate, not proof that a claim is invalid.

exceptions.title: Identifier mismatch
exceptions.symptom: Member, provider or claim identifiers do not agree.
exceptions.example: The member identifier on the draft differs from the source record.
exceptions.action: Compare the values with the authoritative record and confirm which identifier the payer expects.
exceptions.evidence: The source used, fields compared and reviewer decision.
exceptions.avoid: Do not overwrite an identifier solely because another system displays a different value.

exceptions.title: Authorization scope question
exceptions.symptom: Services, dates or units may fall outside an applicable authorization.
exceptions.example: The proposed service date is outside the dates shown on the received authorization.
exceptions.action: Check the authorization, amendments and payer guidance. Resolve the difference with the billing owner before deciding on a correction.
exceptions.evidence: Authorization version, covered period and applicable payer rule.
exceptions.avoid: A populated authorization field does not establish that the service is authorized.

exceptions.title: Claim format or required field
exceptions.symptom: A required field, structure or value format appears incomplete.
exceptions.example: A required provider field is blank in the claim file.
exceptions.action: Identify the claim format and submission route, then check the current implementation and payer requirements.
exceptions.evidence: The field, source requirement and validated correction.
exceptions.avoid: A format check alone does not establish payer acceptance.

exceptions.title: Payer requirement mismatch
exceptions.symptom: The claim appears inconsistent with an applicable payer instruction.
exceptions.example: A referral reference does not match the applicable payer's required format.
exceptions.action: Confirm the payer, program and effective date. Record the exact source section and have the billing reviewer decide the next step.
exceptions.evidence: Current source, section, effective period and applicability.
exceptions.avoid: Do not apply a rule from a different program or jurisdiction.

exceptions.title: Transmission or routing gap
exceptions.symptom: There is no confirmed sending record or the destination is uncertain.
exceptions.example: A claim file was generated, but no transport confirmation is available.
exceptions.action: Check the submission route, enrollment and transport evidence before treating the claim as transmitted.
exceptions.evidence: Transport response, destination and correlation reference.
exceptions.avoid: Generating a file does not mean it was submitted.

exceptions.title: Unclear acknowledgment
exceptions.symptom: A received or accepted status lacks a clear sender or meaning.
exceptions.example: The clearinghouse reports receipt, but payer acceptance is not yet confirmed.
exceptions.action: Read the original response, identify its sender and match it to the correct submission attempt.
exceptions.evidence: Original response, sender, timestamp and claim correlation.
exceptions.avoid: Clearinghouse receipt is not proof of payer approval or payment.

exceptions.title: Remittance or deposit mismatch
exceptions.symptom: Claim lines, adjustments, remittance and cash cannot be reconciled.
exceptions.example: A remittance is available, but its deposit has not been matched.
exceptions.action: Compare the claim and remittance at the appropriate level, then reconcile the deposit separately. Keep unexplained differences open.
exceptions.evidence: ERA/EOB, adjustment detail and deposit reference in the secure system.
exceptions.avoid: Remittance information is not proof that cash reached the bank.

exceptions.title: Unclear follow-up owner or deadline
exceptions.symptom: An unresolved item has no responsible person or verified due date.
exceptions.example: A correction is waiting, but the applicable filing rule has not been checked.
exceptions.action: Assign an owner, locate the payer's applicable deadline source and agree the next follow-up.
exceptions.evidence: Owner, applicable rule, source date and next action.
exceptions.avoid: Do not use a universal deadline across payers or programs.

exceptions.title: Duplicate or unhelpful alert
exceptions.symptom: An alert repeats an existing check or has no actionable finding.
exceptions.example: The billing team has already verified the item with current evidence.
exceptions.action: Document why no change is needed and distinguish a duplicate check from a false alert.
exceptions.evidence: Prior check, reviewer explanation and rule version.
exceptions.avoid: More alerts do not necessarily mean more useful work.

checklist: Confirm scope
Identify the payer, program, jurisdiction, service period, claim format and submission route.
Locate source records
Confirm the required referral, authorization, invoice and service evidence are available in the approved secure system.
Compare identifiers
Check member and submitting provider identifiers against the appropriate authoritative record.
Review authorization evidence
Where applicable, compare services, dates and units with the received authorization and current payer instructions.
Check claim fields
Review required fields, dates, units and modifiers against the applicable claim format and payer rules.
Verify the rule source
Confirm the program, source section, effective period and any relevant updates.
Resolve review questions
Have a billing reviewer decide corrections and document any unresolved exceptions.
Retain transmission evidence
Keep the actual sending confirmation and correlation reference. A generated file is not a submission.
Read acknowledgments
Identify the sender, status and submission attempt for each response.
Assign follow-up
Record the next action, owner and payer-specific deadline source in your secure workflow.
Reconcile remittance and cash
Match claim and line details to the ERA/EOB, then reconcile the bank receipt separately.
Close with evidence
Confirm the documented outcome before closing an item. Silence alone does not establish denial or payment.

states.label: Draft
states.evidence: Claim data or a file has been prepared.
states.meaning: The claim is ready for review within your process.
states.limit: There is no evidence of external transmission yet.
states.next: Review the source information and applicable payer requirements.

states.label: Transmitted
states.evidence: The sending system has recorded transport evidence.
states.meaning: A submission attempt was made through the identified route.
states.limit: Sending does not establish acceptance or adjudication.
states.next: Match the correlation reference and look for the receiving party's response.

states.label: Acknowledged
states.evidence: An identified sender reports receipt or a validation result.
states.meaning: You have a response from a specific point in the route.
states.limit: A clearinghouse acknowledgment is not necessarily payer acceptance.
states.next: Check who sent the response and whether it accepts or rejects the claim.

states.label: Accepted for adjudication
states.evidence: The payer's response indicates acceptance for processing.
states.meaning: The payer can move the claim into its decision process.
states.limit: Acceptance is not approval of payment.
states.next: Track the payer's decision and retain the claim control reference.

states.label: Rejected
states.evidence: A sender identifies a rejection and its details.
states.meaning: The identified submission needs investigation before it can proceed.
states.limit: A pre-adjudication rejection is different from an adjudicated denial.
states.next: Review the reason, correct according to applicable instructions and preserve the original attempt.

states.label: Adjudicated
states.evidence: The payer has issued a claim or line-level decision.
states.meaning: The decision may include an allowance, denial or adjustment.
states.limit: A decision alone does not establish a reconciled bank receipt.
states.next: Review the decision and any applicable follow-up or appeal path.

states.label: Remittance available
states.evidence: An ERA or EOB explains the payer's claim or line-level results.
states.meaning: You can reconcile payment information and adjustments.
states.limit: The remittance does not by itself prove that cash reached the bank.
states.next: Match the remittance to the claim, then reconcile the relevant deposit.

states.label: Cash reconciled
states.evidence: A receipt has been matched to the relevant remittance.
states.meaning: The payment is accounted for in your reconciliation process.
states.limit: A received payment does not show what caused it or whether it is incremental revenue.
states.next: Resolve any remaining differences and close only the supported items.
